messages:
incident-bot: Pager: GPU_POOL_EU_WEST_1 exhausted — queue growth > 10k, avg latency > 3s, severity: P2. Possible autoscaler misfires. Incident channel created: #incidents. Ops runbook: https://redwood/ops/runbooks/gpu-capacity

sara (oncall): ack — I'm on call. grabbing dashboards. tagging eng-sre.

miguel (sre): I'm in. quick snapshot: pool eu-west-1/gpu-pool-1 at 100% alloc, autoscaler reports current_replicas=12, max_replicas=12. scale_up attempts at 02:14:03 and 02:16:21 failed w/ "quota exceeded" from provider. provider logs show transient 429s. Queue depth trace: steady climb from 1.2k -> 11.8k in 6m.

lee (runtime): in the logs I see the autoscaler controller failing to reconcile due to a mis-evaluated predicate: cooldown window considered active because last_scale_time incorrectly set (epoch ms vs s) in one code path. That prevents ramp beyond max_replicas even when provider returns capacity. Posting log excerpt:

```
2026-03-15T02:16:21Z autoscaler: scaleUpAttempt failed: provider quota 429
2026-03-15T02:16:21Z autoscaler: last_scale_time=1610000000000 (ms)
2026-03-15T02:16:21Z autoscaler: now=1700000006 (s)
2026-03-15T02:16:21Z autoscaler: cooldown remaining computed negative -> treated as active
```

miguel (sre): thanks — that explains the misprediction. For immediate mitigation we can: 1) temporarily bump max_replicas to 30, 2) enable eu-west-1 burst pool (if capacity available), 3) failover low-priority queues to eu-central-1. Which should we try first?

sara (oncall): do 1 and 2 now. i'll coordinate failover on queues after we stabilize.

lee (runtime): executing change: `rtr patch autoscaler gpu-pool-1 --max 30` -> running. Deploy-bot response: deploy-bot: autoscaler config update queued (change id: 9f7a).

deploy-bot: update applied: autoscaler.max_replicas=30 (change id: 9f7a).

miguel (sre): enabling burst pool: `provider-cli reserve-burst eu-west-1 --pool gpu-burst-1 --units 100` -> returns success but throttled initially, now provisioned 24 GPUs. Attaching to pool.

anjali (support): customers reporting slow responses on /v1/generate in EU. No data loss, just higher latency and rate-limited responses. Top affected tenants: acme-inc, stello.ai (rate ~ 4% error spike for acme-inc).

tom (customer-ops): notified account managers for acme-inc and stello.ai. telling them we're scaling and will follow up in 30m.

miguel (sre): after bump and burst attach, queue dropped from 11.8k -> 1.6k in ~9min. token latency back to ~800ms for warm requests. Observability shows autoscaler still has the cooldown bug; we need to patch controller.

lee (runtime): opening hotfix branch now. root cause: mixed time unit for last_scale_time persisted as ms in a legacy migration. Fix: normalize to seconds and add unit tests for 32/64-bit int conversions. Deploy plan: small hotfix to controller, can do canary in eu-west-1, should be safe.

miguel (sre): temporary mitigation is in place. I'm keeping an eye on provider 429s. If they return, we should route lower-priority inference to other regions and throttle non-critical background jobs.

sara (oncall): agreed. scheduling manual rate-limit rule for background jobs for next 45m: `route set priority=low -> eu-central-1` and adding throttling header on background worker clients.

anjali (support): opening support thread per affected customer with current status, ETA for full resolution ~45-60m.

lee (runtime): hotfix PR: https://redwood/pull/4809. Includes test and migration check. I'm requesting fast-track review. Asking @miguel and @sara for canary signoff.

miguel (sre): reviewing now. code looks straightforward. after merge let's canary to a small pool (gpu-pool-1a) then roll to rest.

sara (oncall): canary approved. proceed.

deploy-bot: canary deployment started (canary id: c-20260315-01).

deploy-bot: canary success. metrics stable for canary instances. proceeding with rollout.

deploy-bot: rollout complete. controller version bumped to v2.4.7-hotfix.

miguel (sre): post-rollout check: autoscaler now scales properly; verified a synthetic scale test from 0->25 replicas works and cooldown is respected correctly. Queue stable ~300-600 items, latency steady.

sara (oncall): incident moving to mitigated. keeping channel open for 1h for followups. Great work.

anjali (support): sent follow-up to affected customers with explanation and mitigation timeline.

--- POST-INCIDENT NOTES (added by sara):

sara (oncall): timeline summary:
- 02:12 incident triggered: queue climb >1k/min
- 02:14 first scale attempts hit provider 429s -> autoscaler unable to expand beyond max_replicas=12
- 02:18 detected autoscaler cooldown mis-eval (ms vs s) -> hotfix developed
- 02:22 temporary max_replicas bump & burst pool attach -> queue drain started
- 02:35 hotfix canary -> success
- 02:42 rollout complete -> fully mitigated

action items (owners + ETA):
- MIG-1 (lee): add unit + integration tests to catch time-unit mismatches in autoscaler (ETA: 2026-03-20)
- MIG-2 (miguel): add provider-429 backoff + retry policy at autoscaler layer and circuit-breaker (ETA: 2026-03-25)
- MIG-3 (sara): update runbook to include explicit step to check provider quota/429s before bumping max_replicas (ETA: 2026-03-18)
- MIG-4 (anjali): create customer-facing postmortem template and send to affected accounts (ETA: 2026-03-16)
- MIG-5 (platform): schedule chaos test for autoscaler under mixed-timeunit legacy state and provider 429s (ETA: 2026-04-01)

lee (runtime): I'll land the tests and follow-up PRs. noted on the chaos test.

miguel (sre): I'll draft the autoscaler retry/circuit-breaker design doc and drop in eng-ops repo.

anjali (support): will send finalized customer comms once MIG-4 done.

sara (oncall): closing incident in 1h unless regression. tagging @everyone who helped — :tada: nice run.

incident-bot: Incident transitioned to MITIGATED. Severity downgraded to P3. Channel will auto-archive in 72h.
